{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVaC1p88AAAABa35uVA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BpEKozhEdock", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BpEKo", "number": 22, "title": "Implement the complete base SNES hardware in RTL and run it in WebRTL", "body": "## Problem

WebRTL can already compile a real P65C816 RTL CPU, exercise a small memory bus, and render a CPU-programmed BG1 tile pattern (#16, #18, #20). However, those are intentionally restricted demonstrations, **not a complete Super Famicom/SNES**.

Instead of another narrow PPU feature, make **one ambitious end-to-end implementation attempt** to integrate the **entire base SNES console hardware** as synthesizable RTL and run it inside the existing browser-only WebRTL application. This is a large undertaking; do not mark it complete on the strength of a partial demonstration.

## Expected outcome

A selectable **SNES** example in WebRTL that:
- compiles/loads the assembled RTL hardware into WebAssembly in the browser (using the existing client-side toolchain or justified extensions);
- accepts a locally supplied, legally redistributable SNES ROM without uploading it to a server;
- runs the **actual RTL CPU + PPU + APU + console peripherals** together;
- displays the PPU output via Canvas, plays APU-generated audio via Web Audio, and accepts keyboard/gamepad controller input;
- executes and renders at least one independently verifiable homebrew/test ROM through the normal cartridge/CPU/PPU/APU/controller path.

**Scope means the base console**, including its internal chips and their normal interactions—not every optional enhancement coprocessor implemented by cartridges (SA-1, Super FX, etc.), analog/electrical transistor characteristics, or perfect commercial-game compatibility.

Keep WebRTL general purpose; SNES is a demo/RTL project, not a dedicated SNES emulator implemented in JS.

## Hardware implementation scope (single consolidated effort)

Reuse the existing adapted P65C816 where appropriate and evaluate suitably licensed upstream FPGA SNES cores before writing everything from scratch. Integrate or implement, as required:

- **CPU/system bus:** 65C816 with SNES 5A22-style bus and timing behavior, 24-bit address decoding, memory mapping/mirroring, reset vectors, timers, NMI/IRQ, interrupts, controller/auto-joypad registers, multiplication/division and required system I/O.
- **Memory/cartridge:** 128 KiB WRAM, 64 KiB VRAM, OAM, CGRAM, 64 KiB audio RAM and a cartridge ROM mapping path, at least LoROM with HiROM when necessary for the declared base-console scope. Support ROM data provided by browser memory without recompiling the whole HDL per ROM; never send ROMs to a backend.
- **PPU1/PPU2:** backgrounds and tile maps, SNES BG modes including Mode 7, sprites/OAM, palettes, windowing, color math, scroll/priority, scanline/frame sequencing, VBlank/HBlank and CPU-visible registers. Reuse the Canvas output path without a JS PPU or prerecorded image.
- **DMA/HDMA:** transfer registers and timing/interactions with CPU and PPU/WRAM.
- **APU:** SPC700 + S-DSP, CPU/APU port communication, sound RAM, timers, voice/sample processing and PCM output connected to the existing Web Audio pipeline. No browser-side sound synthesis replacing the RTL DSP.
- **Inputs and runtime:** controller shift-register protocol, keyboard/gamepad adapter, video/audio synchronization, Run/Pause/Reset, bounded batching and performance instrumentation.

Use actual, documented RTL interfaces. If imported upstream sources require conversion (e.g. VHDL to supported RTL), preserve provenance/licensing and make adaptations reproducible. Preserve or deliberately improve the established Yosys/CXXRTL/Clang/WASM browser architecture.

## Integration and validation

- Add the SNES example with its source set, top module and board adapter to the current WebRTL project and static GitHub Pages build. Improve limits/ROM loading/clock handling only as needed and document the costs.
- Create small, **original or explicitly redistributable** machine-code/graphics/audio test ROMs and deterministic automated checks covering CPU execution, bus mapping, PPU register writes and rendering, DMA/HDMA, interrupts, SPC700/DSP audio, controller input and reset. Where appropriate, compare against independent SNES specifications or reference emulator traces; do not use copied proprietary ROMs.
- Exercise at least one complete ROM program that takes user input and visibly changes on-screen content **while producing audio** through the RTL system.
- Ensure existing WebRTL counter, video/audio, CPU, and BG1 examples remain functional. Do not let the full console implementation silently replace them.
- Report compile time, generated Wasm size, peak/memory concerns where measurable, simulated master clocks/s, video frames/s and real-time ratio on supported browsers. Browser real-time playability is an optimization goal, **not assumed to be already achieved**.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] A base SNES RTL top-level design contains real integrated CPU, PPU, APU, WRAM/VRAM/CGRAM/OAM/ARAM, DMA/HDMA, controllers and system I/O. There are no placeholder JS emulations for the missing hardware.
- [ ] The integrated design compiles and runs **client-side** from a static `/webrtl/` site or a documented browser-compatible compilation path; source and cartridge data are not uploaded to a compilation server.
- [ ] A locally supplied, openly redistributable ROM runs through the actual RTL cartridge/bus interface, not through an embedded fixed program or prerecorded output.
- [ ] Automated browser/runtime tests verify CPU instructions and reset/interrupts, relevant memory maps, the implemented PPU modes/sprites/priority, DMA/HDMA, SPC700/DSP output and controller effects against documented expected outcomes.
- [ ] A complete integration test runs an original homebrew ROM, verifies that controller input changes the produced frame, checks PPU pixel values and non-silent APU-generated PCM, and resets/repeats deterministically. Validation must be machine-checkable; no manual play/listen gate.
- [ ] The supported **base-console feature matrix** explicitly enumerates CPU/PPU/APU/DMA/I/O coverage and states any limitations. Do **not** close as “full SNES” with essential blocks missing; record unsupported cartridge enhancement chips separately.
- [ ] Licensing, source provenance, reversible/reproducible adaptations, architecture and resource/performance measurements are documented. Existing example regressions pass.

The scope is intentionally **one large, end-to-end Issue**, not a request for the next tiny incremental tile feature. Implementers may use internal checkpoints and linked PRs as needed, but **close this Issue only after the complete acceptance criteria are met**. If the browser toolchain cannot yet handle the full RTL, document and address the actual blockers rather than substituting a software SNES emulator or claiming success from partial PPU output.

## Optional validation

- Benchmark on multiple desktop browsers and improve enough for real-time gameplay if feasible.
- Try publicly distributable compatibility-test ROMs and compare CPU/PPU/APU behavior against a reference emulator.
- Extend support to additional LoROM/HiROM layouts and optional cartridge enhancement chips after the base hardware works.

## Required post-merge verification

After publishing, run automated checks against the **live GitHub Pages site** to confirm the SNES example loads, compiles/starts, executes the test ROM, reacts to controller input, and delivers the expected frame/audio output. Record real results separately. Publication checks are not pre-merge approval gates.

## Related

- #3 — WebRTL general project vision
- #10 — Browser video and audio outputs
- #14 — CPU bus/ROM/RAM test harness
- #16 — Real P65C816 CPU RTL
- #18 — CPU-to-PPU backdrop
- #20 — CPU-programmed BG1 tile rendering
